capex.item: An energy efficient motor was installed in the PM3 hydra pulper, resulting in a power saving of 16 kw.
A new unwind stand at PM1&2 and a vibrating screen in the PM2 broke system were commissioned to boost CHM sheeter capacity.
A ropeless tail feeding system was installed at PM4 to automate tail threading.
A CD caliper profile control system was implemented at PM4 to improve reel building, increase moisture content and reduce fibre…
The MMD drive system and AC01 controller at PM4 were upgraded.
The Maruishi ream packing machine was successfully commissioned to support higher sheeting production.
A new Salvage Winder has been successfully commissioned for providing flexibility in production processes.
A new VAM chiller machine was installed in the Fiber Pulp Mill to achieve energy savings.

bull_bear.body: Prioritizing organic growth via launches; Active BD for land acquisition (outright/JDA); Returning value via ITC divestment (pending final approvals); Maintaining strong balance sheet with minimal debt reliance.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory/Approval Delays (Tower C Worli, Mathura Road); Execution risk on redevelopment projects; Market softening in affordable/mid-income segments; Dependency on timely closure of ITC deal for cash deployment; High land costs in MMR impacting IRRs.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously Optimistic; Disciplined on BD (rejecting low IRR deals); Transparent about approval bottlenecks; Confident in brand pricing power; Focused on cash positivity before margin maximization.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management is intentionally holding back final phases of successful projects (Arika, Trimaya) to act as a hedge against cost escalation and to capture future price appreciation, sacrificing short-term velocity for long-term margin; The INR 60,000 Cr BD pipeline is highly concentrated in MMR (58%), signaling a strategic bet on Mumbai's resilience despite supply concerns.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Debt Profile (Consolidated, as at Jun'26): Outstanding Gross Debt ₹5,824 Cr comprising Short Term Loan ₹718 Cr, Long Term Loan ₹3,866 Cr and Construction Finance ₹1,240 Cr; Net Debt ₹3,438 Cr, with the deck noting Net Debt "* Includes IFC Funding of ₹ 420 Cr". Net debt trend: ₹3,946 Cr (Jun'25), ₹4,226 Cr (Sep'25), ₹3,514 Cr (Dec'25), ₹3,204 Cr (Mar'26), ₹3,438 Cr (Jun'26).
- Net Debt bridge (₹ Cr): Gross Debt 5,824 less Cash and Bank balance 155, Mutual Funds 1,337 and RERA balances 894, giving Net Debt 3,438.
- Credit ratings — ABREL: Non-convertible debentures "CARE and CRISIL AA; Stable"; Commercial paper "CARE and CRISIL A1+". BEPL: Long Term Bank Facilities "CARE and ICRA - AA Stable"; Short Term Bank Facilities "CARE A1+".
- Cash Flow Potential from Launched Projects (data as on 30 June 2026): Pending Collection from Sold Inventories ₹16,203 Cr, Estimated Value of unsold inventory ₹6,917 Cr, Remaining Estimated Project Cost ₹(13,648) Cr (includes partner payout) and Estimated Surplus Cash flow Potential ₹9,471 Cr; launched inventory is ₹31,753 Cr with Total Booking Value ₹24,836 Cr, i.e. "78% of launched inventory", of which ₹8,633 Cr collected.
- Third-party capital at SPV level: IFC invested ₹4,200 Million into residential projects in Pune and Thane covering ~9.5 million sq ft, developed via SPVs with "Birla Estates having economic interest of 56% and IFC 44%"; Mitsubishi Estate Co. Ltd. entered a ₹5,600 Mn joint venture for a premium residential project in Southeast Bengaluru — a 4 million sq ft project via a 51:49 SPV structure and "Mitsubishi's first investment in India's real estate sector".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Residential: Dominant segment with luxury/premium focus (Birla Arika, Niyaara, Trimaya); Commercial: Planning 5 Lakh sqft in Thane (Birla Taranya) and premium spaces in Worli; Redevelopment: Maiden project in Khar (GDV INR 1,700 Cr) signed; Land Bank: Historical lands in Talegaon (45 acres, agri conversion pending) and Kalyan (long-term).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Legacy & Trust": "125-year-old legacy rooted in nation-building since 1897", "Part of the Aditya Birla Group, known for credibility and excellence" and "Entered real estate in 2016 under the 'Birla Estates' brand"; tagline "Legacy-Led. Execution-Driven. Future-Ready."
- Diversified Portfolio: "Portfolio spread across India's top 4 high-growth markets: MMR, Bengaluru, NCR, and Pune" with "Strong presence in premium residential; scaling up commercial portfolio strategically"; the deck notes city-wise sales contribution of "64% share from the markets that we are present in".
- Customer Focus: "Strong recall in premium and luxury segments", "Trusted for quality, design excellence, and transparency", "Poised to be among India's most aspirational real estate brands".
- Superior Design & Execution: "Superior new age design capabilities in all our projects", "Execution anchored in speed, scale, and precision"; the Worli masterplan is "designed and planned by globally recognized architects and designers" including Foster + Partners (UK), Sasaki Associates (USA), LERA (USA), Coopers Hill (Singapore), BPI Design (Singapore) and Priedmann (UAE).
- Market backdrop cited (Propequity): "Buyer preferences continue to shift towards premium, well-connected, and lifestyle-oriented developments, accelerating the ongoing trend of market consolidation in favour of trusted developers."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Divestment] "Divestment of Century Pulp & Paper (CPP) to ITC Ltd." — "Structured as a slump sale for ₹34.98 Bn (subject to adjustments)", agreement signed 31st March 2025 and "Divestment concluded on 01 August 2026". Rationale: "Strategic portfolio realignment to focus on real estate", "Enhances capital allocation and operational clarity" and "Unlock long-term shareholder value". The Q1 FY27 highlights slide separately records the "Sale and transfer of the Company's Pulp and Paper undertaking operated under the name of 'Century Pulp and Paper' was concluded on 01 August 2026 to ITC".
- [Identity] The company is "Aditya Birla Real Estate Limited (formerly Century Textiles and Industries Limited)", CIN L17120MH1897PLC000163, registered at Century Bhavan, Worli, Mumbai; listed as BSE Scrip Code 500040 and NSE Scrip Code ABREL. Real estate development is carried out under Birla Estates / BEPL (Birla Estates Private Limited), whose credit ratings are disclosed separately from ABREL's.
- [Segment reporting] The consolidated Q1 FY27 P&L splits "Continuing Operations" from "Discontinued Operations", with PAT from discontinued operations reported separately — i.e. pulp & paper results are no longer inside the continuing (real estate) line items.
- [Accounting policy] "The company follows a completed contract method for real estate accounting. Net RE income recognized for the quarter will depend upon the projects completed in that quarter" — so reported income is lumpy and not a read on sales momentum.
- [Market data] Sector statistics in the deck are sourced from Propequity: FY2026 pan-India absorption INR 8,99,027 Cr against launches INR 9,52,829 Cr; Q1 FY27 absorption INR 2,36,726 Cr against launches INR 2,21,222 Cr. Across the four markets ABREL operates in, "Total supply ... has dropped by 12% but the corresponding absorption has increased by 6%", with YoY price growth of MMR 1.7%, Pune 5.4%, Bengaluru 8.3% and NCR 8.2%.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Cost pressures managed via phased launches; Construction spend FY27 guided at INR 1,200 Cr; Pricing power evident in Bengaluru (+13.9% YoY) and MMR (+7.4% YoY); Strategy to delay final phases (e.g., Trimaya, Arika Tower 7) to maximize pricing in appreciating markets.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: No specific % guidance given; Margin: Targeting healthy IRRs rather than fixed margin %; Order Inflow: Aiming to launch INR 9,000 Cr+ new inventory in FY27; Capex/Commissioning: Pure construction spend guided at INR 1,200 Cr for FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total GDV ~INR 72,000 Cr (INR 31,700 Cr launched, ~70-75% sold); Unsold inventory ~INR 7,300 Cr; Q4 Presales INR 4,288 Cr; Full Year FY26 Presales INR 8,136 Cr.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: INR 60,000 Cr BD pipeline (MMR ~INR 35,000 Cr); Potential conversion of large deals in FY27; Senior living project in Talegaon; Commercial expansion in Thane and Worli; ITC deal proceeds to fuel acquisitions.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: ABREL delivered a record Q4FY26 with INR 4,288 Cr presales (+69% QoQ) driven by luxury launches in NCR and MMR, though FY27 guidance remains conservative due to regulatory approval bottlenecks for key Mumbai projects. The impending closure of the ITC deal and a robust INR 60,000 Cr BD pipeline position the company for scale-up, provided execution risks on Tower C (Worli) and redevelopment timelines are managed.

Intensified competitive pressure expected in the Indian virgin tissue segment in FY27 due to new entrants, potentially challenging pricing dynamics and market share.

drhp.business: The Company operates primarily in residential real estate development, offering premium and luxury apartments, villas, and plotted developments in major Indian cities including Mumbai, Gurugram, Pune, and Bengaluru. It also holds a Pulp and Paper business (Century Pulp and Paper) which is in the process of being sold to ITC Limited as a going concern on a slump sale basis, allowing the Company to concentrate on its core real estate growth opportunities.
